questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Specifically for Brisbane check out Westella, the social life and people living there during my exchange semester were amazing. Also it's a decent location and not too expensive compared to other options. The landlord seems kind of crazy and very strict though.
Stay away from Scape. The big student accomodations in Brisbane are in general a scam and way too expensive. Scape is additionally run down and a little disgusting.
If you don't get a spot at Westella or want slightly more privacy/space/peace look in to renting a room or sharing a house with someone. this seems to be way cheaper than the student accomodations and you get better accomodation as well.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Public transport is cheap and on campus living is crazy expensive, so off campus is probably the way to go. I can recommend buying a bike (facebook marketplace is a great place to do so) and taking the citycat.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Lots of great clubs and opportunities. One critic is anything affiliated with UQ sport was expensive. The clubs that weren't a part of UQ sporst were way cheaper (*had fair prices*), frankly it seems like UQ sport is a bit of a money machine, making as much as possible from students.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
My personal favourites were:
UQ surfers (surfing society that organised several weekend surfing/beach trips)
QUEST (exchange society that organised pub nights every week, pub crawls and weekend trips. The go to place to mix with all the other groups of exchange students)

I also enjoyed being a part of:
The ultimate frisbee club
The unidive diving club
The fintech club and their poker night
The maths society
The computer science society

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
UQ surfers (surfing society that organised several weekend surfing/beach trips)
QUEST (exchange society that organised pub nights every week, pub crawls and weekend trips. The go to place to mix with all the other groups of exchange students)

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Make sure to attend as many QUEST events and other society weekend trips as possible, especially at the start. That is the best way to meet fellow exchange students and have a lot of fun. Also while you might expect to get a lot of Australian friends, this is not necessarily the case, much more likely you'll enter a bit of an exchange bubble. AND THIS IS OKAY. In the end this might be much better, you'll meet tons of people who just like you have chosen to go on an exchange and are ready for a lot of experiences and fun.
Also some great spots to check out:
Kgari
The Whitsundays
Waterfalls and diving in the Cairns area
North Stradbroke (just a busride and a short ferry trip away from Brisbane)
Moreton Island (go sandboarding on the sanddunes and snorkeling at the shipwrecks)
Sydney
Uluru
New Zealand

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Don't be afraid to focus on meeting other exchange students rather than locals. It might seem stupid to go all the way to Australia and just talk with other Europeans, but my experience was there were some very valuable friendships to be made there. If you really want to meet some Australians, sign up for some of the clubs that aren't popular among the exchange students. For instance some of the more classic sports clubs or academic societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Australia is a nanny state. They have signs every telling you what to do, don't have faith in their citizens and don't expect them to think for themselves. It's kind of a controlling country, with a twisted legal system, big fines for ridiculous things and meanwhile they let other things go.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The friendliness and open attitude of so many people.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Check out Westella for accomodation.
Make sure to engage with the exchange community and get a friend group (there is a lot of interaction across the whole exchange community, but its important to have your base, your close friend group, the ones you'll go on trips together with, share tents on weekend trips with etc.)
Try and avoid having classes on Fridays, many weekend trips start already Friday morning.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: You can get free dinner at the UQ union "kampus kitchen" every night at 17:00. This is a great way to save money, make life easier and catch up with your friends every day.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The amazing friends I made in the exchange community.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I believe that will come when I go home and realise how much money I have spent.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
